title: In the Morning Sow Thy Seed
description: In the Morning Sow Thy Seed in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 1003 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Active Benevolence”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the morn-ing sow thy seed, Nor at eve with-hold thy hand; Who can tell which may suc-ceed, Or if both a-like shall stand, And a glo-rious har-vest bear, To re-ward the sow-er's care?

lines: In the morning sow thy seed,
Nor at eve withhold thy hand;
Who can tell which may succeed,
Or if both alike shall stand,
Sow it 'mid the haunts of vice —
Burst, as in the northern clime
Spring, with all its verdant race,
And his grace shall crown the deed;
He hath said, the precious grain
Never shall be sown in vain.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
